Applications

One engine.
Three worlds to keep alive.

The same probabilistic core closes the loop whether it lives in a fish tank, a poisoned aquifer, or a lunar habitat.

01
Aquaculture · RAS & aquaponics

Healthy by design.

Recirculating systems live on thin margins of oxygen and ammonia. Terra models the nitrogen cycle in real time and steers the system before water quality collapses.

For hatcheries, recirculating systems, offshore operations, and environmental monitoring.
02
Restoration · site intelligence

Restore living balance.

Contaminated and degraded sites need evidence, not promises. Terra estimates contaminant drawdown and infers the microbial community driving recovery — from sparse, drifting sensors.

For field sensing, ecological recovery, bioremediation, and adaptive management.
03
Closed-loop habitats · BLSS

Carry life anywhere.

On the Moon and Mars there is no operator and a 3-second downlink. Habitats must run themselves. Terra closes the coupled biogeochemical budget autonomously — keeping crews alive.

For bioregenerative life support, controlled agriculture, and autonomous habitat systems.

How it works

Live in a day.
Paying for itself in one.

Incumbents sell monitoring — alarms on single sensors. Terra reads the whole system, forecasts failure, and can act. Here's what a deployment looks like.

STEP 01

Install in a day

A small on-site unit, wired to the sensors you already have or a low-cost kit. No cloud, no new build.

STEP 02

Learn your loop

The engine calibrates to your system's true state — automatically compensating for a drifting or fouled probe.

STEP 03

Forecast & act

It warns hours before a failure — or doses and adjusts on its own, behind an autonomy gate with an audit log.

STEP 04

Documented ROI

After a 60–90 day pilot you get a hard number: losses avoided and chemicals, water, energy and labor saved.

Runs offline Your data never leaves the edge No cloud required Autonomy gate + audit log

of what we save.

Terra Platform

Intelligence rooted in the real world.

Rugged edge hardware combines sensor fusion, biological-state estimation, predictive models and local actuation in one adaptive control layer.

STEP 01

Observe

Collect high-resolution environmental and biological data at the edge — raw, imperfect, and continuous.

STEP 02

Predict

Model risk, drift and system behavior with a full Bayesian stack, before thresholds are crossed.

STEP 03

Act

Control pumps, valves, dosing, aeration and circulation locally — closing the loop in milliseconds.

STEP 04

Learn

Improve decisions continuously as the system changes, without ever phoning home.

Simulation

A living model of
every system.

Before Terra acts, it simulates. A probabilistic digital twin runs thousands of futures — sampling the posterior over a system's true state, so every decision is weighed against uncertainty rather than a single guess.

Digital twin · live ESS 0000 Posterior sampling · HMC / NUTS

Digital twin

A continuously updated model of the real system, calibrated to live sensor data.

Posterior over state

Not a point estimate — a full distribution of what's really happening, with honest uncertainty.

What-if in milliseconds

Simulate an intervention before committing to it, on the edge device itself.

Drift-aware

The twin knows its sensors degrade, and re-weights the evidence accordingly.

Proof

Not a demo.
Validated on real data.

The core inference stack is already validated on real biogeochemical data — the same HMC/NUTS engine and process model, applied to a closed Hawaiʻi-island biogeochemical budget from real satellite observations, through the founder's PhD.

It's open for your technical team to read and run. Every fit ships with convergence diagnostics — split-R̂ and effective sample size — so you see the uncertainty, not just a number.

Roadmap

One engine,
retargeted three times.

Terra starts where a loop fails fastest and someone already pays to keep it alive — then climbs. Each Earth deployment hardens the same engine for the next.

Now · Beachhead

Aquaculture

Land-based salmon RAS — sensor-dense, acute pain, no regulatory gate. A strong standalone business and the closest analog to a space habitat.

bench demo 2026 · pilots 2027
Next · Expansion

Bioremediation

An autonomous rover performs and verifies the cleanup — moving Terra into the ~$130B remediation services market as a grant-funded credibility play.

~$130B services market
Endgame · Mission

Life support

Bioregenerative life support for lunar and Mars missions, where autonomous control is the only viable mode — a gap NASA has, in writing, named as unfilled.

$4–5B → ~$10–12B by 2033

FAQ

Questions,
answered.

No. The full inference stack is compiled to run on the edge device itself. There is no cloud dependency and no downlink required — which is exactly what makes it work on a remote site or an off-world habitat.

Pumps, valves, dosing, aeration and circulation — locally, in milliseconds. Terra doesn't just read sensors; it acts on a calibrated belief about the true state of the system.

Recirculating aquaculture and aquaponics, remediation and restoration sites, and closed-loop habitats. The same probabilistic core adapts across all three.

Drift and biofouling are modeled as part of state estimation. The engine knows its sensors degrade and corrects for it, rather than trusting a raw reading.

Yes — Terra nodes are open and extensible, so you can deploy, adapt, and trust them across environments.
